content: To reduce hospital readmissions among individuals with diabetes, several evidence-based strategies have been identified: 1. Scheduled Home Health Visits: Regularly scheduled visits by home health professionals can play a critical role in managing diabetes effectively. These visits allow for close monitoring of the patient’s condition, timely adjustments to treatment plans, and education on self-management practices, thereby reducing the likelihood of complications that could lead to readmission. 2. Ambulatory Follow-Up Care: Ensuring that patients have early follow-up appointments after hospital discharge is essential for maintaining continuity of care. These appointments provide an opportunity to address any emerging issues, optimize glycemic control, and reinforce adherence to prescribed therapies, all of which help prevent readmissions. 3. Targeted Outreach Programs: Programs specifically designed to identify and support high-risk individuals are crucial. For example, patients with a history of diabetic ketoacidosis or those with poorly controlled diabetes, as indicated by an A1C level greater than 9% (>75 mmol/mol), can benefit from targeted interventions. These programs may include intensive education, frequent monitoring, and personalized care plans to mitigate risks. 4. Transitional Care Model: Adopting a transitional care model that emphasizes collaborative, patient-centered approaches, such as medical homes, can significantly reduce readmission rates.
